title: Turn a graph question into a bounded query
description: Choose the business question, graph model, starting anchor, and traversal shape. The workbench exposes model fit, the Neptune query language, illustrative fan-out, and the index behavior to verify before production.

workloads.label: Fraud-ring investigation
workloads.detail: Trace transfers, devices, and accounts from one investigated account.
workloads.question: Which accounts are connected to this account through two or three meaningful relationships?
workloads.fitReason: The request starts from an operational entity and follows typed edges while retaining properties such as amount, timestamp, and risk score.

workloads.label: Standards-based data catalog
workloads.detail: Combine vocabularies, named graphs, and externally governed identifiers.
workloads.question: Which governed datasets satisfy a class-and-predicate pattern across named sources?
workloads.fitReason: RDF preserves global identifiers, triples, named graphs, and standards-based semantics that SPARQL can match directly.

workloads.label: Service dependency impact
workloads.detail: Walk upstream and downstream runtime dependencies during an incident.
workloads.question: Which customer-facing services can be reached from this failed dependency within three hops?
workloads.fitReason: The question is an application traversal over typed dependencies with operational properties such as environment and criticality.

models.label: Property graph
models.detail: Vertices and directed edges can both carry properties.

models.label: RDF graph
models.detail: Subject-predicate-object statements use IRIs and can be grouped into named graphs.

anchors.label: Exact entity ID or IRI
anchors.detail: Bind one known account, service, or resource before walking relationships.
anchors.indexBehavior: A bound subject can use the default SPOG index prefix instead of discovering every possible starting statement.

anchors.label: Selective label and property
anchors.detail: Start from a measured set such as one tenant's high-risk accounts.
anchors.indexBehavior: The engine still has to resolve the property pattern. Confirm selectivity and the chosen plan with explain or profile.

anchors.label: Broad class or label
anchors.detail: Start from every account, service, or dataset in the graph.
anchors.indexBehavior: A broad seed multiplies every later hop. Reframe the request around a selective identity, partition, tenant, class, or time boundary.

paths.label: Named outgoing relationship
paths.detail: Follow one known predicate or edge label from source to target.
paths.indexBehavior: Known subject and predicate values align with the default SPOG access path.

paths.label: Named incoming relationship
paths.detail: Find sources that point to the current entity through one known relationship.
paths.indexBehavior: Binding the predicate keeps the reverse lookup narrower than asking Neptune to discover every relationship type.

paths.label: Any incoming relationship
paths.detail: Walk backward without naming an edge label or RDF predicate.
paths.indexBehavior: Without OSGP, Neptune can union-scan the POGS index across distinct predicates. OSGP can help this shape, but it must be enabled on an empty cluster and adds write and storage cost.
